evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解; oracle graph analysis
evidence.text: The database analyzes the oracle form as an eye (目) inside an enclosing outline, representing a face; it reports face as the original sense. It says a bronze form of 面 itself is not attested, though 面 occurs as a component in bronze graphs using 𦣻 plus the enclosure. It also reports a Chu-slip form whose enclosure strokes changed toward 臼, and cites 面 ‘face toward’ in 上博楚竹書二《容成氏》簡14. These are source assertions, not direct inspection of the cited artifacts.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 面

evidence.field: 說文解字; 說文解字注; historical dictionary examples
evidence.text: The page gives the Shuowen gloss 顔前也 and its analysis 从𦣻，象人面形. Duan Yucai's note describes the visible left-side enclosure as the face and says 面 extended to facing and, in some expressions, facing away. Its cited classical examples include face in 周禮 and 戰國策, and surface in 韓愈; these dictionary citations identify texts but do not establish when each wording was composed or first written.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary entry and later commentary
evidence.title: 面 miàn — 汉典

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry says the Shuowen form is 麪, glossed 麥末也 (Duan's text has 麥屑末也), analyzed as 麥 semantic plus 丏 phonetic. It says 麵 later became a common writing, and that 玉篇 and 廣韻 identify 麵 with 麪. The dictionary explains the later 麵 spelling as using 面 in the sound position, and reports examples for flour/powder in 後漢書 and 麵 in 南史 and Tang poems. Thus the record supports the older graphic analysis and later 麵 spelling, but does not date the transition or establish that 面’s face-word supplied the borrowed word itself.
evidence.title: A04763 麵 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The 面 entry distinguishes classical face-related uses from flour/food senses listed under 面麵、麪. For the flour sense it cites 麪，麦末也 from 說文; separate face entries cite 周禮, 戰國策, and later literature. This is evidence that modern dictionaries treat the flour graph/word history separately, but it is not a primary corpus search and does not prove the exact chronology of sense transfer or graph borrowing.
evidence.title: 面 miàn — 汉典

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Chinese entry for 面 (secondary transcription of Baxter–Sagart and Zhengzhang systems)
evidence.text: The inspected search result reports 面 ‘face’ as Baxter–Sagart *C.me[n]-s, Middle Chinese mjienH, and Zhengzhang *mens. Local validation found 面 at sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv row 2331 with exactly *C.me[n]-s, mjienH, and *C.me[n]-s. No 麵 row was found in that Baxter–Sagart table. Consequently a component comparison between 面 and 麵 cannot be validated from this local dataset; the two systems’ forms should not be silently conflated. The phonetic relation is explicitly asserted by the Ministry dictionary for 麪’s 丏 and by its later-spelling explanation, but sound history alone does not show that the borrowed flour word originated as the face word.
evidence.kind: secondary phonological reference with local dataset verification

gaps: No glyph image was visually inspected. The graphic account relies on the CUHK database’s written analysis and should not be presented as independent visual verification.
The CUHK database reports no bronze inscription of 面 itself; whether that reflects the surviving corpus or a particular catalog’s coverage remains unverified.
Earliest oracle-bone occurrences are not individually dated here, and the database’s graph interpretation is a modern scholarly analysis rather than a dated gloss on each inscription.
The graph’s early use as a polity name is reported by CUHK with attribution to Xu Zhongshu, but the name’s reading and relationship to the face word are not established here.

The Ministry dictionary confirms the Shuowen gloss and 麥 + 丏 analysis of 麪 and later 麵 spelling, but available evidence does not establish the chronology or mechanism by which 面 became its phonetic form, nor a direct semantic path from ‘face’ to flour/noodles.

The noodle artifact and alleged Eastern Han written noodle record are not evidence that the character 麵 or 面 had that sense at those dates; earliest written use of the food word, flour sense, and noodle sense need separate primary-text verification.

The current official Unihan pages for U+9762 and U+9EB5 could not be opened. Local readings were checked, but external click-through verification is unavailable; the exact-record citations are therefore not treated as verified external evidence.

No directly verified primary source supplied a sound reconstruction for 麵 in the same reconstruction system as 面. The local Baxter–Sagart dataset has a row for 面 but none for 麵; do not use the secondary Zhengzhang *meːns as though it were Baxter–Sagart. The independently recoverable name/pronunciation of any depicted oracle object is not established, though 面 is analyzed as a face graph rather than as a whole-graph phonetic loan.
